chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who testified upon the testimony of another man. So the man came and said, 'I did not appoint him as a witness.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of the more just of the two is valid, but if the more just of the two is only one, his testimony is not valid due to fairness between them.'

key_terms.أَعْدَلِهِمَا: the more just of the two

ai.seo_question: How is a single witness's testimony validated if the subject denies appointing them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *Tahajjuz* (partial acceptance) in Shia jurisprudence, where the testimony of the more just (*A'dal*) party prevails when a single witness is disputed. It highlights the scholarly nuance that mere justice (*'Adalah*) is insufficient if the opposing party is equally or more just, thereby preventing unilateral validation in cases of doubt. This rule underscores the Shia emphasis on evidentiary balance and the rigorous evaluation of witness credibility in legal proceedings.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who testified upon a testimony of another man. So the man comes over, so he said to him, ‘I did not (appoint him) as a witness (on my behalf)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who is more just from the two would be allowed (to give testimony), but if (there is only) one just (to be found), his testimony would not be allowed in fairness to both of them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from b Sinan who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man who bears testimony to the testimony of another witness but then the man says that he had not appointed him as witness.

Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The testimony of the one who is more just is admissible but if such man of justice is one man then his testimony is not acceptable because of fairness for both.’”
